fields.label: Description
fields.value: Comparing a freshly computed digest with a trusted expected digest to detect data changes.

record.name: Integrity verification
record.description: Comparing a freshly computed digest with a trusted expected digest to detect data changes.
record.label: Integrity verification

fields.label: Purpose
fields.value: Detect modification or substitution of downloaded content.

fields.label: Steps
value: Obtain the expected digest from an authenticated/trusted source.
Compute the digest of the received file with a suitable modern algorithm.
Compare values using the correct algorithm and encoding.
If a mismatch occurs, reject or investigate the file; if it matches, interpret the result only within the trust model.

fields.label: Caveats
value: A digest posted beside a file on the same unauthenticated channel may be replaced together with the file.
A matching hash does not prove that software is benign or that the publisher is trustworthy.

fields.label: Name
fields.value: Parse and interpret a v1 .torrent file

fields.label: Summary
fields.value: Decode bencoding, read the info dictionary, interpret single-file or multi-file layout, and use piece hashes to verify payload chunks.

value.action: Read the .torrent byte stream and decode its bencoded top-level dictionary.
Read announce if present, plus optional extension fields such as announce-list, url-list, httpseeds, nodes, and private.
Read info.name and either info.length for a single file or info.files entries for a multi-file torrent.
Read piece length and split the logical content stream into pieces; multi-file v1 content follows files-list order.
Interpret pieces as concatenated 20-byte SHA-1 digests, one digest per piece.
Calculate the v1 infohash over the exact bencoded info dictionary and use it for torrent identity.
Use trackers and/or DHT to discover peers, fetch pieces, verify them, and assemble the payload.
